result.topic_en: Gauss sets up recursive formulas for paraxial ray tracing through a system of refracting surfaces (sign conventions for curvature, reduced distances inside the glass) and derives the abscissa and ordinate of the image point.

$x$ \quad $y$ \quad $\left\| \begin{matrix} \frac{\alpha'''}{\beta'''} + t \\ \frac{\gamma'''}{\delta'''} + u \end{matrix} \right| \begin{matrix} [-t-] t\beta'''y \\ u\delta'''\frac{y}{x} \end{matrix}$

$\# h\frac{n-1}{nr} + h''$
$hf + h''(f + f' + f'')$
$hf + h''f'''$

$\frac{1}{\beta'''[-\delta'''-]} = t\,\beta'''x - \delta'''$
$t = \frac{1}{\beta'''(\beta'''x - \delta''')}$
$\alpha'''\beta'''x - \beta'''\gamma''' [-\ldots-]$
$\frac{\alpha'''x - \gamma'''}{\beta'''x - \delta'''} = \mathrm{Absc.}$
$\frac{y}{\beta'''x - \delta'''} = \mathrm{Ord} = \eta$
$y = \eta(\beta'''x - \delta''')$
